speciesDescription: The green sea turtle is a large sea turtle of the family Cheloniidae. It is the only species in the genus Chelonia. Found in tropical and subtropical waters around the world, it is known for its herbivorous diet and long migrations.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical oceans, coral reefs, seagrass beds
distribution: Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans

speciesDescription: The loggerhead sea turtle is a marine turtle found throughout the world. It is characterized by its large head and powerful jaws, which it uses to crush hard-shelled prey.
distribution: Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans

speciesDescription: The hawksbill sea turtle is a critically endangered sea turtle belonging to the family Cheloniidae. It is the only species in its genus and is recognized by its distinctive beak-like mouth.
habitat: Coral reefs, rocky areas, shallow coastal waters
distribution: Tropical Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans

speciesDescription: The leatherback sea turtle is the largest living turtle and the fourth-heaviest modern reptile. Unlike other sea turtles, it lacks a hard shell, instead having a leathery skin over its back.
distribution: All tropical and temperate oceans

speciesDescription: The olive ridley sea turtle is the smallest and most abundant of all sea turtles. It is known for its mass nesting events called arribadas, where thousands of females come ashore to lay eggs simultaneously.
distribution: Tropical Pacific, Indian, and Atlantic Oceans

speciesDescription: Kemp's ridley sea turtle is the rarest and most endangered species of sea turtle. It is one of two species in the genus Lepidochelys, the other being the olive ridley.
habitat: Shallow coastal waters, Gulf of Mexico
distribution: Gulf of Mexico, Atlantic coast of North America

speciesDescription: The flatback sea turtle is a sea turtle endemic to the continental shelf of Australia. It is the only species in the genus Natator and is named for its flattened carapace.
distribution: Northern Australia, Papua New Guinea

speciesDescription: The red-eared slider is a semiaquatic turtle native to North America. It is the most popular pet turtle in the world and has been introduced to many other regions through the pet trade.
distribution: Central and eastern United States, introduced worldwide

speciesDescription: The painted turtle is the most widespread native turtle of North America. It lives in slow-moving fresh waters and is recognized by its colorful markings on its head, neck, and shell.
distribution: North America from Canada to Mexico

speciesDescription: The common snapping turtle is a large freshwater turtle of the family Chelydridae. It is known for its powerful jaws, aggressive temperament when out of water, and long tail.
distribution: Southeastern Canada to Florida, west to Rocky Mountains

speciesDescription: The alligator snapping turtle is the largest freshwater turtle in North America. It is known for its powerful jaws, spiked shell, and a worm-like appendage on its tongue used to lure fish.
diet: Fish, frogs, snakes, other turtles, plants
distribution: Southeastern United States

speciesDescription: The eastern box turtle is a terrestrial turtle found in the eastern United States. It is known for its hinged plastron that allows it to completely close its shell for protection.
distribution: Eastern United States

speciesDescription: The diamondback terrapin is a species of turtle native to the brackish coastal marshes of the eastern and southern United States. It is the only North American turtle adapted to saltwater habitats.
distribution: Atlantic and Gulf coasts of the United States

speciesDescription: The spiny softshell turtle is a species of softshell turtle native to North America. It has a leathery, flexible shell and a long, snorkel-like snout.
habitat: Rivers, lakes, ponds with sandy bottoms
distribution: North America from Canada to Mexico

speciesDescription: The Chinese softshell turtle is a species of softshell turtle native to East Asia. It is widely farmed for food in China and is also found in Japan, Korea, and Russia.
distribution: China, Japan, Korea, Russia, introduced elsewhere

speciesDescription: The Galápagos tortoise is the largest living species of tortoise and can weigh over 400 kg. It is native to the Galápagos Islands and is famous for its role in Charles Darwin's theory of evolution.
distribution: Galápagos Islands, Ecuador

speciesDescription: The Aldabra giant tortoise is one of the largest tortoises in the world. It is endemic to the Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles and can live for over 100 years.
diet: Grasses, leaves, woody plant stems, fruits
distribution: Aldabra Atoll, Seychelles

speciesDescription: The African spurred tortoise is the third-largest species of tortoise in the world and the largest mainland species. It is native to the southern edge of the Sahara Desert.
distribution: Southern Sahara Desert, Sahel region, Africa

speciesDescription: The Russian tortoise is a small tortoise species native to Central Asia. It is a popular pet due to its small size, hardiness, and friendly personality.
distribution: Central Asia, Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, China

speciesDescription: The Greek tortoise is a tortoise species found in North Africa, southern Europe, and the Middle East. It is one of the five Mediterranean tortoise species.
distribution: North Africa, southern Europe, Middle East

speciesDescription: Hermann's tortoise is a small tortoise species native to southern Europe. It is named after the French naturalist Jean Hermann.
distribution: Southern Europe, Balkans, Turkey

speciesDescription: The radiated tortoise is a tortoise species native to southern Madagascar. It is considered one of the most beautiful tortoises in the world due to its star-patterned shell.
distribution: Southern Madagascar

speciesDescription: The Burmese mountain tortoise is a large tortoise species native to Southeast Asia. It is one of the few tortoise species that incubates its eggs in a nest.
distribution: Southeast Asia: Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia

speciesDescription: The Indian star tortoise is a tortoise species native to India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. It is named for the star-like patterns on its shell.
distribution: India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka
